transport_experiment.question: does Ollama honour options.num_ctx on each endpoint?
transport_experiment.consequence: model.ollama_num_ctx in Hermes config.yaml is a no-op against Ollama over /v1, even though Hermes correctly maps it to extra_body.options.num_ctx in plugins/model-providers/custom/__init__.py. The only fixes are outside the harness: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, or PARAMETER num_ctx in a Modelfile.
transport_experiment.generality: independent of model size and of GPU; affects any model served to any harness over the OpenAI-compatible wire
transport_experiment.no_native_transport: Hermes has no native Ollama /api/chat transport in its chat loop; grepping the source finds only a Slack URL, a web upload route, and a comment in plugins/model-providers/custom/__init__.py:59 noting /api/chat honours a field the OpenAI wire drops (ollama#14820). Every chat request leaves over /v1, so no value of any Hermes setting can raise the served context.

upstream_bug.summary: the guard fires only when _ollama_num_ctx < 64000, which is the context Hermes requested, not the context the server loaded
upstream_bug.effect: with a model advertising 262144, the guard never fires, and its helpful message (naming the model, base URL and the exact fix) is replaced by 'Context length exceeded (34 tokens). Cannot compress further.'
upstream_bug.aggravating_detail: Ollama returns the real value as n_ctx:4096 in the body of the 400, and the very next log line reads 'provider did not report a max context length; keeping context_length at 262,144 tokens and compressing'. The value was parsed and discarded.
upstream_bug.suggested_fix: read n_ctx off the exceed_context_size_error body and use it to correct the cached context length before deciding to compress
upstream_bug.classification: bug in the diagnosis path, not in the agent loop
